prompt: Multiply two non-negative numbers given as digit strings using schoolbook long multiplication, one digit pair at a time. Complete multiply without parsing the operands into int or long.
explanation: Multiplying an a-digit number by a b-digit number never needs more than a + b digits, so a scratch int array of that size can hold the whole answer. The pair of digits at positions i and j contributes to result slot i + j + 1, with any carry landing in slot i + j -- letting the nested loops accumulate into the array means you never have to add long partial products together. The final pass strips leading zeros, taking care to leave a single "0" when the product really is zero.
hints: Allocate int[] digits = new int[a.length() + b.length()]; a product can never be longer than that.
Multiply a.charAt(i) - '0' by b.charAt(j) - '0', add whatever is already in digits[i + j + 1], then keep the ones place there and add the carry into digits[i + j].
When you build the string, skip the leading zeros -- but if you skipped them all, the answer is "0".
